proof: Any convex aggregation lies between its minimum and maximum input. Every observed long element mean exceeds every observed short mean. Any nonempty long subset retains minimum≥176.1; arbitrary one-short deletion cannot increase maximum beyond152.0. Thus any assignment of these element means to nonempty bird groups and any nonnegative normalized within-bird weighting preserves the gap.
scope: Observed element means only; not per-rendition support, population effect, raw individual-bird estimate, p-value, or identification of a tutor-specific comparator.
